mark-ring.note: The lighter half of the mark's source pair (public/qmanager-mark.svg). Not consumed directly as a UI fill: its hue drives the dark-mode primary-container and the active-nav tone. Changing it is a system-wide change, not an asset tweak.

primary-light.note: The mark's tail, used literally. Brand, the only action accent, focus, active nav, 5G NR identity.

secondary-light.note: 4G LTE identity. Never acts. Chosen at 296 so it cannot read as a tone of the brand blue.

tertiary-light.note: Counts, upload direction, minor accents. Never acts. Low chroma on purpose.

success-light.note: Healthy: connected, service active, save succeeded, profile applied. Paired with CheckCircle2Icon.

warning-light.note: Degraded: weak signal, searching, limited service, partial success. Retuned from L 0.75, which measured 2.4:1 on white and failed AA.

destructive-light.note: Failed or irreversible: disconnected, apply failed, reboot dialogs. Paired with XCircleIcon or AlertCircleIcon. Ring tone steps --tone-destructive-1/2/3 now ship in both themes (light 0.945 0.05 25 / 0.905 0.08 25 / 0.835 0.12 25; dark 0.275 0.07 25 / 0.365 0.105 25 / 0.49 0.15 25), so all three ring ramps are symmetric. The failed service ring used to borrow surface-container, surface-container-high and destructive-container, which is a neutral grey ramp with one red note and read as broken chrome rather than as a red state.

surface-light.note: Cards, dialogs, popovers. Steps: background, surface, surface-container, surface-container-high. All neutrals carry a trace of the mark's hue.

display.purpose: The h1 at the top of every feature page. 700 weight, 30px. Page titles only.

headline.purpose: Large card titles and state labels. 600 weight, 20px.

title.purpose: The CardTitle default. 600 weight, 16px, leading-none so titles align with adjacent metadata.

body.purpose: Default UI text, descriptions, table cells. 400 weight, 14px.

metric-row.purpose: The dense metric-row step: 13px at 600 weight on a 20px line box, written text-[13px]/5, used for both label and value of a pill metric row on a glance card. Shipped on both dashboard Primary Status cards (components/dashboard/signal-status-card.tsx). The explicit /5 leading is load-bearing: 13px is an arbitrary Tailwind size and would otherwise inherit the card's leading, and pinning the line box to 20px is what holds the row at exactly 40px so the loading skeleton's h-10 keeps mirroring it. Do not use 13px outside a dense metric row; 14px body and 12px label remain the defaults.

label.purpose: Chips, table headers, button text, form labels, 11px uppercase sidebar section labels. 500 weight, 12px.

numeric.purpose: Live signal values, counters, timers. 600 weight, always tabular-nums so values do not jitter as they tick. SIZED TO SLOT: this is the one step that is deliberately not a fixed ramp, because a numeral's job is to be read at the distance its container implies, and a figure that fills its tile is doing something the 14px body step cannot. The size is therefore derived from the slot that holds it, not chosen from the ramp, and a literal text-[Npx] on a tabular-nums numeral is correct by construction rather than a ramp violation. Shipped steps, all Geist Mono: 52px live throughput and 44px live latency in the Speed Test dialog's running phases (components/dashboard/speedtest-dialog.tsx), where the numeral is the entire content of a tonal block and the comp's whole idea is that the number is the interface; 26px in that dialog's three result tiles, sized so three tiles fit one row without wrapping; 17px with an 11px unit suffix in the dashboard's Speed Test tile (components/dashboard/live-latency.tsx), where the pair is sized to the tile's 34px action row and is LOAD-BEARING — SPEEDTEST_TILE_H mirrors that height into LiveLatencySkeleton, and the card crossfades skeleton over content, so re-sizing the figure onto the ramp reflows the tile and makes the handoff visibly jump; 11px for the mono relative timestamp in the same tile. A numeral that is NOT sized to a slot still takes the ramp: prose, labels and units that stand alone do not qualify, which is why that tile's phase name ('Download') is text-xs and not the comp's 11px. Do not use this step to smuggle arbitrary sizes onto non-numeric text.

mono.purpose: Geist Mono. AT terminal, logs, CopyableCommand, IMEI/ICCID, ARFCN, dBm readouts. Never decoration.

pre-auth-card.purpose: Surface-scoped exception for the two pre-auth screens ONLY (/ the Overview splash and /login/), sanctioned by the Login and Overview comp. Five steps: card title 19px (text-[1.1875rem], tracking -0.01em); section title 17px (text-[1.0625rem]); emphasis 15px (text-[0.9375rem]) for the 48px pill CTA label and status-tile values; body 13px (text-[0.8125rem]) for subcopy, field labels, inline errors and banner body; eyebrow 11px (text-[0.6875rem], tracking 0.11em uppercase). Every other screen sits inside the app shell, where the sidebar, page title and card grid establish scale before a card speaks; these two are the only screens that are a single card on an empty canvas, so the card must build five levels of hierarchy from nothing inside ~400px of width, where the 14px/12px default flattens to two. The comp draws the eyebrow at 10px; it ships at 11px because that is the floor already set by the sidebar exception and by the eyebrow the Overview card shipped before the retarget, and going lower would make uppercase text at 0.11em tracking the smallest type in the product. Both surfaces share the 48px pill CTA role, so these steps change on both screens in the same commit. No other surface may use them.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Optional card lift in light theme. Never load-bearing; depth is tonal. Absent in dark.

shadows.name: popover-float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers. The 'not part of the page flow' signal, and the only real shadow in the system.

motion.name: emphasized
motion.purpose: Container size and shape changes, aggregation chain re-proportioning, banner arrival, page-level enter. In code: ease-emphasized plus --duration-emphasized. This is the ceiling, not a starting point.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Nav indicator translate, card entrance, meter fill, chip container morph. In code: ease-standard plus --duration-standard.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Label swaps, live value ticks, hover tints, focus rings. In code: ease-quick plus --duration-quick.

motion.name: ambient
motion.purpose: Service rings, live ping dot, spinners. In code: ease-ambient plus --duration-ambient. The only loops in the product, one per surface, only where something is genuinely live.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: The card cascade step, as --stagger-step. Wider and the last card feels late behind a slow poll. Curves live in @theme and emit Tailwind utilities; durations are plain custom properties, because Tailwind v4 has no --duration-* theme namespace.

motion.name: ca-meter-fill
motion.purpose: Meter fill on first paint only (Motion Guide recipe 07). The keyframe carries a `from` and deliberately no `to`, so it animates up to whatever scale the element inline transform already holds: the correct end state stays in the DOM and the keyframe describes only the journey. That is the Non-Load-Bearing Rule satisfied literally. Do not substitute a requestAnimationFrame-armed state flip; rAF does not fire in a backgrounded tab and would strand every meter at zero. Subsequent polls move the scale through a transition rather than replaying.

motion.name: ca-segment-enter
motion.purpose: A carrier the radio just ADDED grows in from zero width, on the same open-ended keyframe construction as the meter. Scoped to genuine additions only: a whole chain appearing at once is the card arriving, which belongs to the skeleton handoff, and four simultaneous width animations would be four layout passes to announce something that was never absent. Width is the single sanctioned width animation in the product, because here the width is the data.

motion.name: skeleton-handoff
motion.purpose: Crossfade with no movement (Motion Guide recipe 03). The outgoing skeleton is an overlay ON TOP of the real content, never a sibling beside it: stacked as siblings the container sizes to the taller of the two for the duration of the fade and then collapses, so the handoff ends on a jolt. As an overlay the content owns the container height from its first frame and the crossfade contributes no layout shift. Render the skeleton from one extracted definition shared by the loading branch and the overlay, or the two drift and the Skeleton-Mirror Rule fails silently.

motion.name: value-tick
motion.value: opacity 1 to 0.35 to 1, 180ms ease-out (Web Animations API)
motion.purpose: The live value tick, implemented as TickingValue (components/ui/ticking-value.tsx) over useValueTick. WAAPI rather than a keyed remount, so it does not churn the DOM inside a polling surface aria-live region, and so a value moving mid-dip interrupts and retargets instead of queueing behind the device. Fires on change and never on first paint; arrival belongs to the skeleton crossfade. The one place reduced motion removes an opacity change rather than preserving it, because a repeating luminance flash every two seconds carries no information the new number is not already carrying. Requires tabular-nums.

iconLibraries.name: Material Symbols Rounded
iconLibraries.scope: Sidebar navigation, the dashboard route (every dashboard card body), the two pre-auth routes / and /login/, and the /cellular/ INDEX (Cellular and Radio Information) only. Self-hosted subset (app/fonts/MaterialSymbolsRounded-subset.woff2, 71 glyphs, 26.4 KB), never a CDN link. The /cellular/ extension is PARTIAL and tracked: the index is converted, its 17 sub-routes (Cell Scanner, Band Locking, SMS Center, APN Management, Antenna Alignment and the rest) are still lucide, so a lucide glyph under /cellular/ outside the index is correct code and must not be 'fixed' one route at a time. FILL 1 for the active nav item, FILL 0 for inactive. The boundary is per-route, not per-component: the failure the rule prevents is two icon sets inside one screen. MaterialSymbol sets fontSize inline, so parent auto-sizing utilities such as badge.tsx [&>svg]:size-3 cannot reach it; every call site passes `size` explicitly. Adding a glyph means editing the single canonical list MATERIAL_SYMBOL_NAMES in components/ui/material-symbol-names.ts (kept sorted), then re-running `bun run icons:subset` and committing the WOFF2 and its manifest .json together. MaterialSymbolName is derived from that array and the subset generator imports it, so the type and the font cannot disagree; `bun run icons:check` runs inside `bun run package` and fails on a stale font, an unsorted list, or a collapsed FILL axis.

iconLibraries.name: Lucide
iconLibraries.scope: Every route still on lucide: the /cellular/ sub-routes (the /cellular/ index is Material), Local Network, Monitoring, System Settings, /setup/ (components/onboarding/**, deliberately out of scope), their dialogs, the header bar, page content. Also the two sanctioned dashboard exceptions on Network Status (CardSimIcon, Plane), and components/auth/change-password-dialog.tsx, which mounts from the authenticated sidebar rather than /login/ and is correct as lucide.

iconLibraries.name: react-icons/md
iconLibraries.scope: Legacy dependency, not to be extended. One sanctioned survivor: the RAT marks on Network Status (MdOutline5G, Md4gPlusMobiledata, Md4gMobiledata, Md3gMobiledata), which are typographic marks Material Symbols has no equivalent for.

iconLibraries.name: Tabler
iconLibraries.scope: Sanctioned secondary for glyphs lucide lacks.

narrative.overview:
QManager is still the calm, expert console an operator trusts when something matters. What changed is how that calm is expressed: color is no longer scarce, it is structured. The system is a real Material-3-style tonal palette derived from the QManager mark, where content sits inside filled tonal containers rather than being sprinkled as colored text on white. Density stays the job; color now organizes the density instead of decorating it.

The aesthetic is tonal at rest, expressive in transition, dense in data, honest in state. A surface tells you what kind of thing it is by its fill and its radius before you read a word of it. Nothing shouts, because everything is a container: hierarchy comes from tone, size, and shape rather than from one loud focal element competing for attention.

It earns its restraint twice, as it always did. Once as a stylistic principle, and again as a safety principle: QManager is served by the modem it manages, so the routine 90% should feel effortless and the risky 10% should feel deliberate. A colorful interface is not permission to become a consumer router app.
keyCharacteristics: OKLCH-only. #000 and #fff never appear as literals; every neutral is tinted toward the mark's hue.
The palette is derived from the mark, not chosen alongside it.
Three identity hues (primary blue, secondary violet, tertiary cyan) plus the functional four. No hue is decorative and functional at the same time.
Euclid Circular B is the interface voice; Geist Mono is the machine voice. There is no third voice.
Depth is tonal. Shadows are optional and never load-bearing.
Motion is expressive in duration and curve, and never overshoots.
Light and dark are first-class equals; dark mode is genuinely colored, not desaturated.
Build on shadcn/ui first and restyle its primitives with these tokens.

rules.name: The Source-Color Rule
rules.body: New colors are derived from the mark's hue family or from an existing identity or functional role. Nobody picks a hue by eye and adds it to globals.css.

rules.name: The Container-Pair Rule
rules.body: Never place text on a role's fill unless you are using that role's -foreground; never place it on a container unless you are using that container's on- ink. Mixing a fill with a container's ink is the single most common way to fail contrast here.

rules.name: The Functional-Color Promise
rules.body: A user who learns green means healthy on the dashboard finds the same green meaning the same thing in Watchdog, in Profile Apply, and in the alert logs. Hue and chroma were retuned; meanings did not move, and functional colors are never decorative.

rules.name: The Identity-Never-Acts Rule
rules.body: Secondary and tertiary carry identity, never affordance. A violet surface means 'this is the LTE leg', never 'click me'. Only primary acts. This replaces the retired One-Accent Rule, whose intent it preserves: exactly one hue acts.

rules.name: The Semantic-Token Rule
rules.body: Reach for bg-success-container and text-on-surface-variant, never raw Tailwind palette classes like text-blue-500. The theme switch depends on it.

rules.name: The OKLCH-Only Rule
rules.body: No hex literals, ever. New colors enter the system in OKLCH form in globals.css; conversion is the author's job, not the consumer's.

rules.name: The Explicit-Tone Rule
rules.body: Layered translucency is banned for stacked shapes. The service rings composite to a flat disc when built from one color at 0.15 / 0.25 / 0.40 alpha; they use four explicit tone steps instead.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Euclid Circular B speaks for the interface; Geist Mono speaks for the machine. There is no third voice. Pairing Euclid with another UI sans is forbidden. An icon font is not a voice and does not count against this rule.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: font-mono is scoped to device output and technical data: the AT terminal, raw log viewers, CopyableCommand, inline code for AT command strings, and identifier or value readouts. It is never reached for as decoration.

rules.name: The Tabular-Number Rule
rules.body: Any value that updates live is tabular-nums. Non-negotiable: a tonal pill makes jitter more visible, not less.

rules.name: The Weight-Discipline Rule
rules.body: 400 body, 500 labels and medium emphasis, 600 headings and numerics, 700 page titles only.

rules.name: The Card-Wrapped Surface Rule
rules.body: The card component owns its whole content (CardHeader plus CardContent with every control); the page only arranges cards. The page is never the layout canvas with cards demoted to fragments.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Two surfaces at different conceptual elevations differ by at least one container step. This is now the only elevation signal in both themes.

rules.name: The No-Hairline-On-Fill Rule
rules.body: Bordered rows inside a tonal card are replaced by container fills. A border is reserved for inputs, for table rules in genuine data tables, and for the outlined-card variant. This replaces the retired Border-Carries-Structure Rule.

rules.name: The Highlight-by-Container Rule
rules.body: Emphasis promotes a surface one container step and changes its ink, rather than adding a translucent wash over a neutral card.

rules.name: The Radius-Follows-Size Rule
rules.body: A surface's radius is a function of its size and role, not of taste. A 28px tile never sits inside a 20px card, and a chip is always fully round.

rules.name: The Fill-Over-Stroke Rule
rules.body: When a shape needs to be distinguished from its neighbor, change its fill, not its border. Borders survive only on inputs and genuine table rules.

rules.name: The Settled-Motion Rule
rules.body: Every transition ends at rest. The save check at 1.03 is the ceiling for overshoot, not the floor. Bouncy, elastic, and rubber-band motion stay banned.

rules.name: The Expressive-Duration Rule
rules.body: Anything that changes a container's size, shape, or fill runs at standard or emphasized. The old 140-160ms floor is retired: at 140ms a container color change reads as a flicker rather than a morph. Value and label swaps stay at quick.

rules.name: The Transform-Only Rule
rules.body: Animations touch opacity and transform, plus color via CSS transitions. The aggregation chain's width is the sole documented exception, and it is data, not decoration.

rules.name: The One-Loop Rule
rules.body: At most one ambient loop per surface, and only where something is genuinely live. A loop that runs while nothing is happening is a lie.

rules.name: The Motion-Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds 400ms. Emphasized is the ceiling, not a starting point, and the only durations longer than it in the product are ambient loops, which are not transitions.

rules.name: The Non-Load-Bearing Rule
rules.body: No transition may be load-bearing: if it never runs, the UI is still correct. This is stronger than the Reduced-Motion Rule, which only covers the user's preference. A transition can also be skipped because the element mounted mid-flight, because the tab was backgrounded, or because a slow poll landed the data before the animation started. Final state is computed and correct on its own; the animation is only how it got there.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: Movement goes, opacity stays, and no layout depends on a transition completing. Because durations are now longer, this matters more than it did.

rules.name: The Loader-and-Dots Rule
rules.body: Step and sample progress is a Loader2Icon spinner plus discrete dot indicators. Fill bars remain data visualization only.

rules.name: The Solid-Container Rule
rules.body: A banner is bg-{role}-container, never a wash. The retired pattern was border-info/30 bg-info/10; a 10% alpha over a tinted surface is not a stable color, its value moves with whatever sits behind it, it collapses to near-invisible in dark mode, and it is the first thing to wash out in sunlight. The container and its on- ink are a measured pair, which is also why the border becomes unnecessary.

rules.name: The Glyph-Disc Rule
rules.body: The banner icon always sits in a filled circle. A bare 16px glyph disappears against a saturated container, and the disc is the element that survives when the container fill washes out. It also makes the banner and the status chip read as the same family.

rules.name: The One-CTA Rule
rules.body: One action per banner. The deferred-reboot role is the single sanctioned exception: 'review what changed' and 'do the risky thing' are genuinely different decisions, so it carries a tonal Review and a destructive-fill Reboot now.

rules.name: The Dismiss-Only-Notices Rule
rules.body: A banner gets an X only when it is a notification. Conditions (stale data, deferred reboot, in progress, degraded) leave when the condition leaves, and never before. Nothing that reports a broken link gets a dismiss affordance. When a notice is dismissible it must be dismissible durably: the SIM-swap banner persists its dismissal server-side in the SIM registry, not in component state.

rules.name: The Info-Is-Brand Rule
rules.body: Informational banners use primary-container, not a separate info hue. The SIM notice and the apply pipeline are the same class of 'the system is telling you something', and the functional four already spend the saturated-blue slot on the brand.

rules.name: The Tabular-Counter Rule
rules.body: Any figure that ticks inside banner copy is font-mono tabular-nums. Without it, '38 s' to '39 s' reflows the whole sentence once a second.

rules.name: The Icon-Boundary Rule
rules.body: Replaces the retired Nav-Glyph Boundary Rule, which scoped Material Symbols to the sidebar alone. Material Symbols Rounded appears in the sidebar nav AND the dashboard route; every other route is lucide. A lucide icon inside a nav item is a bug, and so is a Material Symbol on a route not yet migrated. The boundary is per-route on purpose: the failure it prevents is two icon sets inside one screen, and the dashboard was carrying four (lucide, react-icons/md, /fa6, /tb) beside a Material sidebar. Moving the boundary again is one deliberate change that updates DESIGN.md, this file, and CLAUDE.md together. It does not leak.

rules.name: The Network Status Landmark Rule
rules.body: Network Status keeps its existing icons through any restyle; it is a recognized landmark on the one glance surface and re-glyphing it buys nothing. Two exceptions to the icon boundary survive on it by explicit decision, and they are the only two on the dashboard: the SIM orb keeps lucide CardSimIcon and Plane, and the RAT glyphs keep react-icons/md (MdOutline5G, Md4gPlusMobiledata, Md4gMobiledata, Md3gMobiledata), because 5G, 4G+ and 3G are typographic marks Material Symbols has no equivalent for.

rules.name: The Identity-Chip Rule
rules.body: The Badge variants `nr` (primary-container, brand blue) and `lte` (lte-container, Carrier Violet) are identity roles, not status roles: they say which radio a chip belongs to and never vary with health. The five status roles (success, warning, destructive, info, muted) remain the only correct choice for an actual status indicator. Where a chip carries identity, the quality it also reports must be encoded somewhere non-chromatic. On the dashboard Primary Status cards that channel is the Material glyph bar count: signal_cellular_4_bar (excellent), signal_cellular_3_bar (good), signal_cellular_2_bar (fair), signal_cellular_1_bar (poor), signal_cellular_off (none) — the constant-silhouette wedge family, not the alt bar family the mock drew, whose lower rungs are non-monotone in ink mass. That is a stronger channel than the fill ever was, since success-container and warning-container measure 1.03:1 apart.

rules.name: The Explicit-Sizing Rule (Material glyphs)
rules.body: MaterialSymbol renders a span and sets fontSize as an inline style, which outranks any utility. Parent auto-sizing rules that reach a lucide child do not reach it: badge.tsx [&>svg]:size-3 and empty.tsx [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-6 both silently lose. Every Material glyph passes `size` explicitly at its call site (12 in a dense chip, 16 where the glyph is the only channel carrying meaning, 24 in an EmptyMedia). Only pointer-events ports across, via a parallel [&>[data-slot=material-symbol]] rule.

rules.name: The Service-Ring Axes Rule
rules.body: Network Status orbs run two orthogonal axes that must stay distinct. RING TONE tracks RAT quality: amber is a working connection that is not optimal (LTE without carrier aggregation), not a fault. CORE GLYPH tracks service liveness. The shipped table is green+pulse+check (Optimal), amber+pulse+check (LTE without CA), amber+static+warning (Searching / Limited), red+static+priority_high (No Service / SIM error / unknown). The pulse is a redundant channel gated by isServiceActive: prefers-reduced-motion removes it and the glyph carries the meaning alone. Tone says how bad, motion says whether it is alive, which is what keeps a full-strength red ramp from crying wolf.

rules.name: The Filled-Chip Rule
rules.body: Every status indicator is a filled tonal chip: a role container fill, that container's on- ink, an icon, and pill radius. This replaces the retired Outline-Badge Rule. If a chip needs to feel louder, the answer is a banner or an alert, not a stronger fill.

rules.name: The No-Header-Icon Rule
rules.body: CardHeader is CardTitle plus CardDescription only. Icons live in chips or in the CardAction slot. Once one card grows a header icon, every card grows one.

rules.name: The Save-Button Singleton
rules.body: All save actions use SaveButton plus useSaveFlash. Extend it rather than fork it.

rules.name: The Consistent-Layout Rule
rules.body: Feature pages compose as a page header plus a uniform container-query grid of self-contained cards. A bespoke asymmetric layout unique to one screen is almost always wrong.

rules.name: The Skeleton-Mirror Rule
rules.body: Loading skeletons reproduce the geometry of the loaded state, radius included; the page must not reflow when real data arrives.

rules.name: The Saved-State Honesty Rule
rules.body: Surfaces describing live behavior tell the truth: status cards render saved settings and actual daemon state, the dashboard flags stale data instead of freezing silently, a released carrier stays visible and greyed rather than vanishing, and the apply dialog renders 'Preparing...' rather than a fabricated step list.

rules.name: The Muted-vs-Destructive Rule
rules.body: Muted means 'deliberately off' (Stopped, Disabled, Offline peer). Destructive means 'failed' (Disconnected link, Failed email). Muted must stay genuinely grey so the two never blur.

rules.name: The Deferred-Reboot Rule
rules.body: Nothing reboots the modem as a side effect. Reboot-requiring changes surface an explicit dialog or an in-pipeline heartbeat notice; persistent conditions get a banner.

dos: Do derive new colors from the mark's hue family or an existing role, in OKLCH, as tokens in globals.css.
Do pick a pair: a fill with its -foreground, or a container with its on- ink. Never mix across.
Do use filled tonal chips with an icon for every status indicator.
Do keep the functional four meaning exactly what they meant before.
Do use pill metric rows on glance surfaces (12 rows or fewer) and hairline rows in genuine data tables.
Do carry elevation with a container step, and let shadows be optional.
Do scale radius with surface size: 28px inner tiles, 36px cards, 40px hero surfaces, full-round chips and nav.
Do animate container changes at standard or emphasized, and value or label swaps at quick.
Do build stacked shapes from explicit tone steps, never from stacked alpha.
Do keep tabular-nums on every live value and font-mono on machine output and identifiers.
Do keep Material Symbols Rounded inside the sidebar and the dashboard route, lucide on every other route, and self-host the Material subset rather than linking Google's CDN.
Do pass `size` explicitly on every MaterialSymbol; its inline fontSize outranks the parent's auto-sizing utilities.

Do add a new glyph to MATERIAL_SYMBOL_NAMES in components/ui/material-symbol-names.ts, keeping the array sorted, then re-run `bun run icons:subset` and commit the regenerated WOFF2 and its manifest .json in the same change. A name the type permits but the font lacks ships the literal word on a modem in the field; `bun run icons:check` fails the build if the font is stale.
Do encode quality non-chromatically (bar count, glyph ladder) whenever a chip's fill is spent on identity.

Do keep metric value tints on the functional palette for both radios, using the darkened -on-surface ink steps (5.88 / 5.95 on surface-container in light) rather than the solid role tokens (4.29 / 3.74, both below AA), and add an sr-only quality word after each tinted value.
Do test both themes, and measure the worst text pairing on each new surface before merge.
Do keep CardHeader to title plus description, and put icons in chips or CardAction.
Do use SaveButton for saves and exactly one filled primary action per surface.
Do compose feature pages as a page header plus a uniform container-query card grid, and author each card as a self-contained component the page arranges.
Do build on shadcn/ui first; restyle its primitives with these tokens rather than hand-rolling.
Do use container queries inside a card that declares @container/card, and keep viewport breakpoints for page-level decisions.
Do render step and sample progress as a spinner plus dot indicators; keep fill bars for data visualization.
Do make skeletons mirror the loaded layout, put table empty states inside the table, and surface stale data with an honest alert band.
Do defer reboots behind explicit dialogs or in-pipeline notices with honest time expectations.
Do include aria-label on icon-only buttons, role=status or aria-live on polling surfaces, and role=alert on failure bands.
donts: Don't use hex literals, #000, or #fff. Every color enters as an OKLCH token.
Don't place text on a fill using a container's ink, or on a container using a fill's foreground.
Don't use outline-and-tint status badges. (Retired rule: the Outline-Badge Rule.)
Don't treat secondary or tertiary as an action color, or as a second brand. (The One-Accent Rule is retired as written; its intent survives as the Identity-Never-Acts Rule.)
Don't animate a container color, size, or shape in 140ms. (Retired rule: the 140-160ms floor.)
Don't add overshoot beyond the sanctioned 1.03 save check; no bounce, no elastic, no rubber band.
Don't stack translucent copies of one color to fake tonal layers.
Don't put pill rows in a 60-row table, or hairline rows on a four-row glance card.
Don't reintroduce a hairline border on a card that already carries a tonal fill.
Don't add icons to CardHeader. They drift into hero-metric SaaS template territory.

Don't put a Material Symbol on a route still on lucide, a lucide icon inside a nav item, or re-glyph Network Status while restyling it. (Retired rule: the Nav-Glyph Boundary Rule, which scoped Material Symbols to the sidebar alone.)
Don't use the `nr` or `lte` Badge variants for a status indicator. They say which radio, never whether it is well.
Don't tint a metric value by radio identity, and don't tint an identifier row (Band, ARFCN, PCI, SCS) at all: an identifier has no good-or-bad reading to announce.
Don't load an icon font or webfont from a remote CDN; the modem serves this app and may have no internet.
Don't introduce a second UI typeface, or hand-wire a font into a component with a font-family style.
Don't use background-clip: text gradients, side-stripe accent borders, or glassmorphism.
Don't ship the hero-metric SaaS template, or invent a bespoke layout for one feature page.
Don't build grids of decorative icon-plus-heading cards that carry no real controls.
Don't hand-roll a component shadcn/ui already provides (tabs, accordion, dialog, popover, tooltip, select, dropdown).
Don't let a functional hue be decorative, or a decorative hue land within 40 degrees of a functional one.
Don't mix viewport breakpoints and container queries inside the same card; one breakpoint authority per card.
Don't make modals the first thought. Inline disclosure, destructive buttons with clear descriptions, and deferred banners cover most confirmations.
Don't let a UI claim liveness it does not have: no fake timers, no placeholder step lists, no frozen values without a stale-data notice.
Don't document or reference removed features (NetBird VPN, DPI/Traffic Engine, Low Power Mode daemons) as design surfaces.
Don't use em dashes in documentation.
